item.title: Gian Achen and Clementine Darling — Wed Nov 11, 7:30 PM — The California
item.description:
Gian Achen is a Bay Area artist whose music blends nostalgic melodies with heartfelt lyrics. Gian's sound is rooted in the golden era of '60s rock, drawing inspiration from iconic bands like The Beatles and Creedence Clearwater Revival as well as modern artists such as Wilco and The Shins. Gian's music invites listeners to join him in a world that’s both familiar and uniquely his own. Clementine Darling is an Americana Folk Singer-Songwriter with her heels dug deep in San Francisco Bay Area’s music scene. Originally from Seattle, Washington, Darling busked her way down the West Coast in 2010, on a road trip that led her to put down roots in Sonoma County, California. The two locals influenced her debut 11:11 EP and subsequent Live At The Lost Church— a collection of introspective songs and soulful ballads, with undertones of Seattle 90’s grunge. Doors Open: 6:30 PM | Show Starts: 7:30 PM
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.description:

Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market.
Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. item.title: Nov & Dec Artwalks: "Moments in the Light" Plein Air Painting — Fri Nov 13, 5:00 PM — McCune Collection
item.description:
Plein Air painting is painting on location responding to the environment as it moves you. For us it’s not about the details or exact characteristics of a location but rather the interaction of color, the atmosphere, the feeling of standing out there. It's about the immediate moment of seeing which is in the brushwork of several of the artists, creating a dialogue with the space as you make the marks and see how they correspond to what's in front of you. There is no right or wrong because it is a very personal moment. It's not impressionism. It's not quite expressionism. But it's the immediacy of being alive.
Most of the paintings were done when Barry convinced one of the other artists to come painting with him. Creating a synergy from the overlapping influence on each other while keeping a distinct POV.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Paint & Sip with Genevieve Elkin — Fri Nov 13, 5:30 PM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join us for a relaxed and social paint & sip evening. You'll be guided step-by-step through painting a scenic view using acrylics, with plenty of room to make it your own.
Whether you follow along or add your own creative twist, the focus is on enjoying the process and having fun. Sip on a beverage, come with friends or meet new ones, and settle into a laid-back night of painting and connection. No experience needed - just show up and create.
Genevieve Elkin was Born and raised in Mill Valley, California and is a multidisciplinary artist now based in Petaluma. She earned a BFA in Illustration from Parsons School of Design and has professionally managed art departments, supporting artists and new media on high-profile projects. Genevieve loves painting, drawing, and exploring ceramics, and enjoys helping students experiment, have fun, and develop their own creative voice.
To learn more:@gennaelkin

item.title: Write & Collage: Words, Images & Memory — Sat Nov 14, 10:00 AM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join Marlene Cullen for a creative two-hour experience that brings writing and collage together. In the first hour, guided freewriting prompts invite you to explore memorable moments, stories, and experiences in a welcoming, supportive environment. In the second hour, transform those reflections into a visual expression using images, colors, and textures.
No writing or art experience is necessary—just bring your curiosity and a willingness to explore.
Bring: A notebook and pen. Collage materials will be provided, and you're welcome to bring a favorite poem, magazines, photographs, or other materials you'd like to incorporate.
Marlene Cullen is the founder of Writers Forum and creator of Jumpstart Writing Workshops. Through her website and blog, The Write Spot, she shares resources and inspiration to help writers discover and develop their voices.
The Write Spot anthologies edited by Marlene are collections of short stories, poems, and vignettes with prompts to encourage writing.

item.description:
AI Reality Check by Humans in Control
Date and time: Saturday, November 14 at 11:00 AM
Location: South Annex at The Key Room \(Gilardi Training & Events Center\) · Novato · CA
Join your neighbors for an AI Reality Check, part of a nationwide campaign about what AI means for our jobs, our kids, and our future.
In a short, plain-language presentation, we'll look at what AI really is, the risks it creates, and commonsense steps we can take to keep humans in control. Expect real audience participation, practical ways to take action, and no jargon. You don't need any AI expertise to join. Please register, below!
This talk is hosted by Sophie DeWitt, a Marin County–based program manager with a background in education and advocacy. As a volunteer presenter, she aims to bring these conversations into the community and to make the future of AI something we can all participate in shaping.
Looking forward to seeing you there!

item.title: Nov & Dec Artwalks: "Moments in the Light" Plein Air Painting — Sat Nov 14, 11:30 AM — McCune Collection
item.description:
Plein Air painting is painting on location responding to the environment as it moves you. For us it’s not about the details or exact characteristics of a location but rather the interaction of color, the atmosphere, the feeling of standing out there. It's about the immediate moment of seeing which is in the brushwork of several of the artists, creating a dialogue with the space as you make the marks and see how they correspond to what's in front of you. There is no right or wrong because it is a very personal moment. It's not impressionism. It's not quite expressionism. But it's the immediacy of being alive.
Most of the paintings were done when Barry convinced one of the other artists to come painting with him. Creating a synergy from the overlapping influence on each other while keeping a distinct POV.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Mushroom Foraging — Sun Nov 15, 9:00 AM — The Sea Ranch Lodge
item.description:

Join Ty the Fungi, a seasoned local forager with nearly 15 years of experience, and learn how to find, identify, and responsibly harvest wild mushrooms—from prized edibles to those best left untouched. Discover the principles of ethical foraging and deepen your connection to the landscape through this immersive, hands-on exploration.
Meet at The Lodge’s Fireside Lounge, and we’ll caravan together to the foraging site.
$160 per person, $100 (ages 10-16). Space is limited. This adventure is recommended for participants with moderate to advanced hiking experience.

item.title: Healdsburg Garden Club General Membership Meeting — Mon Nov 16, 1:00 PM — Villa Chanticleer Annex
item.description:
The next General Membership meeting will take place on Monday, November 16, 2026, at the Villa Chanticleer Annex (860 Chanticleer Way, Healdsburg). The meeting begins at 1:00 PM, followed by a light potluck luncheon and an educational program. Guests are welcome.
Our speaker for November is Bruce Horace Robinson, a Sonoma County Master Gardener, Class of 2016. He will give a presentation on "Good Bugs, Bad Bugs." Bruce has been a gardener since childhood. After many years of changing garden strategies, he has become a strong believer in creating a garden that is in balance and harmony with nature by using biological controls and adhering to sustainable gardening principles.
The public is invited to attend this presentation starting at 2:00 PM at the Villa Chanticleer Annex.
